# Quiz image `alt` text is auto-generated and frequently broken (accessibility)

**Upstream**: `oak-openapi` (Oak Open Curriculum API) — quiz content / image
metadata. Canonical intake: the `oak-openapi` `docs/requests/` folder. **Do not
edit `oak-openapi` from this repo** — hand this over.
**Status**: open
**Priority**: high (WCAG 2.2 — 1.1.1 Non-text Content; affects every consumer that
renders or relays quiz images, including assistive-technology users)
**Affected**: the `questionImage.alt` field and answer-option `image.content.alt`
field on quiz data, returned by `GET /lessons/{slug}/quiz` and surfaced through the
MCP `get-lessons-quiz` tool, plus the same images on the Oak website.

## Problem

The `alt` text on quiz images appears to be machine-generated by an image-captioning
model and is, in a large share of cases, **unusable as an accessible text
alternative**. Three failure modes recur, often together:

1. **Repetition loops** — the caption repeats a phrase until it runs out of budget,
   e.g. `"a black and white photo of a black and white photo of a black and white
   photo of …"` or `"…the cell membrane, the cell membrane, the cell membrane, and
   the cell membrane"`.
2. **Hallucination / wrong subject** — the caption describes something the image is
   not, e.g. a food-chain diagram captioned as `"a man standing next to a cow and
   another cow standing in front of a sign that says, cow"`.
3. **Ignores the image's function** — many quiz images are **functional**: the
   question refers to labelled parts (A/B/C/D), a word-summary equation, or a
   labelled diagram, so the `alt` must convey that labelled content for the question
   to be answerable without sight. Instead the caption describes surface appearance
   and omits the labels, making the question impossible for a screen-reader user.

A related issue: **answer-option images** (the pupil-avatar illustrations) carry the
answer text in a separate `text` field, so the avatar image is **decorative** — its
`alt` should be empty (`alt=""`), not a caption of the drawing (which also contains
misspellings such as `"hairdow"`).

Because the MCP server and SDK pass the upstream `alt` field through faithfully, this
cannot be fixed downstream — the fix belongs at the source.

## Evidence (reproducible)

Each row reproduces with `get-lessons-quiz { lesson: <slug>, filter: "images" }`
against the Oak Curriculum MCP (or `GET /lessons/{slug}/quiz` directly). Verified
2026-06-08.

| Lesson slug | Quiz / image | Observed `alt` | Why it fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `photosynthesis` | exit quiz, word-summary image `tvavm8fxdowsffw3kkma.png` | "a black and white photo of a black and white photo of a black and white photo of a black and white photo of a black and white photo of a black and white photo" | Repetition loop; conveys nothing. The image is a word-summary the question asks about. |
| `adaptations-of-plants-for-photosynthesis-absorbing-light` | starter, plant-cell diagram `yhgv4ehofyug9dcu2rrg.png` (Q: "Which part is only found in plant cells?") | "a diagram of the structure of a plant cell, including the cell membrane, the cell membrane, the cell membrane, and the cell membrane" | Repetition loop **and** functional failure — the question needs the labelled parts (chloroplast, nucleus, …); the label content is absent. |
| `adaptations-of-plants-for-photosynthesis-absorbing-light` | starter, arrow image `p0liozzgjskxiqzqrijw.png` | "a black arrow pointing to the right on a white background with a black arrow pointing to the left on a white background with a black arrow pointing to the right" | Repetitive and self-contradictory. |
| `adaptations-of-plants-for-photosynthesis-absorbing-light` | exit, leaf image `fxhioxnzq7jen2ifir1r.jpg` (Q: "Which part of this leaf contains the most chlorophyll? Part A/B/C/D") | "a picture of a plant with the name of the plant below it and a picture of a plant with the name of the plant below it" | Functional failure — the A/B/C/D labels the question depends on are not described; answer is impossible without sight. |
| `adaptations-of-plants-for-photosynthesis-absorbing-light` | exit, answer-option avatars (e.g. `cogzc3hge8eng04ojics.png`) | "a black and white drawing of a woman's head with a turban on top of her head" (another: "…a girl's head with a hairdow on it's head") | Decorative image captioned; answer text is in the option's `text` field. `alt` should be empty. Note misspelling "hairdow". |
| `plant-nutrition` | starter, labelled plant diagram `iiffyis5rhfiditusmz1.png` (match question) | "the parts of a plant labeled in the diagram below are labeled in the diagram below are the parts of a plant labeled in the diagram below are labeled" | Repetition loop; the part labels needed for the match question are absent. |
| `plant-nutrition` | starter, food-chain image `ad37sgmacu4vihwubixt.png` (Q: "How many producers are shown in the food chain?") | "a man standing next to a cow and another cow standing in front of a sign that says, cow" | Hallucination; the food chain the question counts is not described. |

The pattern (repetition, hallucination, function-blindness, decorative captioning,
misspellings) is consistent with an automated image-to-caption model run without
question context or human review. The examples above are a small sample found while
exercising a handful of science lessons — the problem is very likely systemic across
the quiz-image corpus.

## Suggested approach

In rough priority order:

1. **Mark decorative images as decorative.** Answer-option avatar images whose
   meaning is carried by the option `text` should have `alt=""` (empty), not a
   caption — this is the correct WCAG treatment and removes a large class of noise.
2. **Author functional `alt` with question context.** For images the question
   depends on (labelled diagrams, word summaries, charts), the `alt` must convey the
   labelled content / data the question tests. Generation that ignores the question
   stem cannot produce this; the alternative text needs the question context, and
   functional images warrant human authoring or review.
3. **At minimum, fix the generation defects.** Eliminate the repetition loops and
   the obvious hallucinations, and correct misspellings — these are unusable
   regardless of context.
4. **Expose an "alt reviewed" signal** if helpful, so consumers can distinguish
   human-authored/reviewed alt from raw auto-generated captions.

A short style note for authors (functional vs decorative; describe the content the
question tests, not the picture's surface) would prevent regressions.

## Impact

Quiz images are currently inaccessible to screen-reader users in many cases, and the
captions add misleading noise for everyone consuming the data (including AI agents
that relay quiz content). Fixing `alt` at the source makes every consumer — the Oak
website, the MCP/SDK, and assistive technology — accessible at once and meets WCAG
2.2 AA 1.1.1. **Backwards compatibility**: changing `alt` values (including setting
decorative images to `alt=""`) is structurally non-breaking — the field shape is
unchanged.
